title: Source schema
question: Which fields were actually supplied?
sql: PRAGMA table_info(raw_marketing);
interpretation: Seven source columns include an exported index. The index is not a user characteristic or experimental variable.

title: Source coverage
question: What is the analysis unit and how many outcomes exist?
sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) rows, COUNT(DISTINCT "user id") users,
SUM(converted) conversions FROM raw_marketing;
interpretation: 588,101 rows correspond to 588,101 distinct users and 14,843 conversions. No repeated-user aggregation is needed.

title: Missingness
question: Are exclusions needed for missing source values?
sql:
SELECT SUM("user id" IS NULL) user_null,
SUM("test group" IS NULL) group_null, SUM(converted IS NULL) converted_null,
SUM("total ads" IS NULL) ads_null, SUM("most ads day" IS NULL) day_null,
SUM("most ads hour" IS NULL) hour_null FROM raw_marketing;
interpretation: All six meaningful fields are complete. Zero rows are excluded for missingness.

title: Duplicate user IDs
question: Could repeated users violate the independent-user analysis?
sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) duplicate_users, COALESCE(SUM(n-1),0) extra_rows
FROM (SELECT user_id,COUNT(*) n FROM marketing GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*)>1);
interpretation: No duplicate user identifiers were found. Independence still relies on user identity and assignment being correctly recorded; one row per ID cannot verify household or device interference.

title: Outcome and assignment categories
question: Are group labels and binary outcomes valid?
sql:
SELECT test_group,converted,COUNT(*) users FROM marketing
GROUP BY test_group,converted ORDER BY test_group,converted;
interpretation: Only ad/psa labels and 0/1 outcomes occur. Keep both converters and non-converters in the denominator.

title: Range checks
question: Do exposure and time values fit their definitions?
sql:
SELECT MIN(total_ads) min_ads,MAX(total_ads) max_ads,
MIN(peak_hour) min_hour,MAX(peak_hour) max_hour,
SUM(total_ads<0 OR peak_hour NOT BETWEEN 0 AND 23) invalid_rows
FROM marketing;
interpretation: Ads range from 1 to 2,065 and hours from 0 to 23. Large exposure counts are not automatically errors; they remain in the primary comparison.

title: Index audit
question: Is the extra index a usable analytical variable?
interpretation: The index runs from 0 through 588,100. It is dropped during cleaning; there is no evidence it represents time or ordering of assignment.

title: Cleaning reconciliation
question: Did preparation change outcomes or cohort size?
sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) users,COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) distinct_users,
SUM(converted) conversions,SUM(total_ads) impressions FROM marketing;
interpretation: All original users and outcomes are retained. Preparation renames fields, converts the Boolean outcome to 0/1, removes the index and adds derived labels. No outliers are discarded.

title: Allocation
question: How unequal are the observed arm sizes?
interpretation: Ad users represent 96.0000% of observations. Unequal allocation is not itself evidence of failure. A target split must be specified independently; 96/4 is only a diagnostic scenario here.

title: Primary outcomes
question: What are the conversion rates and correct denominators?
sql:
SELECT test_group,COUNT(*) users,SUM(converted) conversions,
AVG(converted) conversion_rate FROM marketing GROUP BY test_group;
interpretation: The ad-minus-PSA difference is 0.7692 percentage points, or 43.09% relative lift. The smaller PSA arm governs most of the precision.

title: Exposure volume
question: How much exposure is associated with each arm?
sql:
SELECT test_group,SUM(total_ads) impressions,AVG(total_ads) ads_per_user,
AVG(CASE WHEN converted=1 THEN total_ads END) ads_per_converter,
AVG(CASE WHEN converted=0 THEN total_ads END) ads_per_nonconverter
FROM marketing GROUP BY test_group;
interpretation: These are descriptive exposure summaries. Exposure may be affected by treatment, behavior and conversion; it cannot safely serve as a pre-treatment adjustment variable.

title: Frequency-band outcomes
question: How does conversion vary with observed exposure?
interpretation: These bands were selected for readability, not optimized for significance. Different exposure bands contain different kinds of users; apparent dose-response does not establish a causal frequency effect.

title: Weekday outcomes
question: How do rates vary by peak-exposure weekday?
interpretation: Weekday means the day with the most ad exposure for that user. It is not the day of conversion, a dated cohort or a randomized scheduling treatment.

title: Hour outcomes
question: What is the observed peak-hour conversion profile?
interpretation: Use counts with rates. Sparse overnight PSA cells have noisy estimates, and selecting the highest observed hour would overstate certainty.

title: Day-hour cells
question: What data support the heatmap?
sql:
SELECT day_order,peak_day,peak_hour,test_group,COUNT(*) users,
SUM(converted) conversions,AVG(converted) rate FROM marketing
GROUP BY day_order,peak_day,peak_hour,test_group
ORDER BY day_order,peak_hour,test_group;
interpretation: All populated day-hour-arm cells are shown. The report heatmap uses ad-arm conversion rates; it is an exploratory exposure-context display, not a scheduling recommendation.

title: Sparse day-hour cells
question: Where should heatmap comparisons be treated cautiously?
sql:
SELECT test_group,COUNT(*) cells,SUM(n<100) cells_under_100_users,
SUM(c<10) cells_under_10_conversions FROM
(SELECT test_group,peak_day,peak_hour,COUNT(*) n,SUM(converted) c
FROM marketing GROUP BY test_group,peak_day,peak_hour) GROUP BY test_group;
interpretation: Low conversion counts, especially in the PSA arm, make fine-grained contrasts unstable. No 168-cell significance search is used to recommend a winning slot.

title: Extreme exposures
question: How concentrated is the long tail?
interpretation: Above the common 99th-percentile threshold (202 exposures), 5,810 users account for 12.99% of all recorded impressions. Retain them for the primary test.

title: Exposure-trim sensitivity
question: Does the sign persist after a common tail exclusion?
interpretation: The trimmed difference is 0.7919 pp. This changes the population using a post-assignment variable; it is an influence diagnostic and cannot replace the full-cohort estimate.

title: Outcome by exposure band share
question: How does the exposure mix differ between arms?
interpretation: Mix differences can explain descriptive patterns but are not baseline randomization balance checks. No pre-treatment covariates are supplied.

title: Counterfactual conversion calculation
question: What would the ad arm produce at the PSA rate?
sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT COUNT(*) n,SUM(converted) c FROM marketing WHERE test_group='ad'),
p AS (SELECT AVG(converted) rate FROM marketing WHERE test_group='psa')
SELECT a.n ad_users,a.c observed_ad_conversions,p.rate psa_rate,
a.n*p.rate expected_at_psa_rate,a.c-a.n*p.rate modeled_incremental FROM a,p;
interpretation: This is a modeled counterfactual, not individually observed attribution. Its causal interpretation requires valid randomization, consistent measurement and no interference.

title: Weekday contrasts with multiplicity
question: Which weekday contrasts remain after a common correction?
interpretation: Intervals are pointwise 95% Newcombe intervals. Segment p-values use two-sided Fisher exact tests, including sparse hourly cells. Holm adjustment controls one exploratory family of 31 weekday/hour contrasts. Conditioning on peak day still limits causal interpretation.

title: Hour contrasts with multiplicity
question: How much does multiple testing change hour-level evidence?
interpretation: Two-sided Fisher exact p-values address within-segment ad-versus-PSA differences, not whether one hour has a larger effect than another. They avoid the small-cell z approximation. Formal interaction diagnostics are separate.
